explanation: The historical Senate reference is +1.1 percentage points Republican minus Democratic, built from 2022, 2018.

The point call uses historical Senate returns only. It is explicitly not an EV-informed call: Current county shares versus historical final candidate-vote shares; this is NOT a same-stage early-voting comparison. Final-result context does not adjust the live point. Each share difference is weighted by that county’s historical R-minus-D margin. It does not reveal how current early voters voted.
assumptions: This is a party-margin research projection, not observed candidate votes, a certified result, or a validated winner probability.

The reference pools different Senate seats, candidates and classes. It is not nominee-adjusted; current ballot identities and incumbency are unverified and no historical candidate is assumed to be running.

Historical reference: up to three earlier Senate-election years of the same election type within 12 years, with a six-year recency half-life. Presidential, midterm and off-year environments are not pooled. Contests in the same state/year receive equal weight.

An EV adjustment requires compatible same-stage early-vote geography from the same election type, method and status definition. Final-election geography remains descriptive context and cannot adjust the live point.
Eligible EV adjustment = 0.35 × the change in county-weighted historical party margin, capped at ±5 percentage points. Both the coefficient and cap remain unvalidated research assumptions.
Current early voters and later Election Day voters can differ sharply. Individual early-voter choice is unobserved; county correlations do not identify it.
The reported range is a deliberately wide, unvalidated sensitivity range, not an 80% or 95% confidence/credible interval.
Polling, party registration and demographic marginals do not enter this initial projection. No unreported age-by-party, religion, propensity or demographic intersections are manufactured.
warnings: Candidate configurations and survey populations are never pooled together.
Historical reconstruction exists; switch evidence mode to inspect its documented basis. It cannot establish what was reported then.
Survey response shares are preserved; undecideds are not reallocated.
Historical published candidate returns are election context, not early votes or contemporaneous reporting snapshots.
Margin is winner lead in percentage points; Democratic margin is D minus R; swing is change in D minus R.
Matching geographic identifiers do not establish identical boundaries across vintages.
The reference is a final candidate-vote distribution, not an equivalent day or voting opportunity in a prior early-voting cycle.

references.title: Census: turnout and early voting in the 2022 midterms
references.lesson: Even midterms differ: both turnout and the share voting before Election Day changed between 2018 and 2022. Match election type, then inspect method and calendar changes.

references.title: EAC: 2024 election administration findings
references.lesson: Early in-person and Election Day are separate voting methods. A rise in one can reflect a timing shift instead of higher final turnout.

references.title: Pew: validated-voter voting-method research
references.lesson: Party-method relationships change. Do not hard-code Republicans as Election Day voters or Democrats as mail voters. This methodological reference supplies no votes or polling adjustment to the model.
